name: Stroke Filter
oneLine: The filter each of us holds up between incoming strokes and ourselves, letting in only the ones that match our preferred stroke quotient - and discounting the rest.
whatYouDid: You watched Rosita deflect a compliment she didn't quite believe ("eh, they're easy tables") and take an over-the-top one too much at face value - the filter runs in both directions, screening out true strokes and letting in flimsy ones.
confusion: People think discounting a stroke is just modesty; the tell is that a discounted stroke never gets banked - it's filtered out specifically because it doesn't match a self-image the person already holds, whether or not that image is accurate.

fromBook.quote: each of us holds up a stroke filter between ourselves and incoming strokes

expand.definition: Your stroke quotient is your personal, mostly unconscious preference for which kinds of strokes - positive or negative, conditional or unconditional, from whom - you'll let in; the stroke filter is the mechanism that screens out strokes which don't fit it.
expand.otherFraming: TA Today draws a sharp line between a filtered-out stroke and a rejected one: openly rejecting a stroke you don't want is clean, but discounting one you do want, because it doesn't fit your self-image, just leaves you stroke-deprived while strokes are visibly being offered.
expand.tryThisToday: Next time you catch yourself saying "oh, it was nothing" to a genuine compliment, stop and just say "thank you" instead - notice the urge to add more.
